I think we might regret name collisions with "history" later anyway, make a call, and we can discuss on the PR 🙂 <@!694014391288332358> I'm ready to pair on that whenever, you have a time in mind? Ready now, lemme ping you Just because I like making names: - `trin-chronicle` - `trin-chain` - `trin-archive` - `trin-annals` - `trin-saga` - `trin-train` is archive not also a name collision? Also, I think it's totally okay to be silly with naming, as long as it's also clear. The holy grail of names is a funny pun that's also actually meaningful. I think trin-saga is fun. But yeah, maybe let's move this to a PR or issue. Everyone in <#796057759858425866> doesn't need our full deliberation 🙂 gotcha, i thought you were renaming the 6 networks that piper posted about a few weeks ago and i got gradually more and more confused as i went down your list haha trin-train: the portal subnetwork for requesting the names of popular trains What was the value of treating them as completely separate DHT networks again? I think I missed that discussion. being able to opt-in to only certain ones, and not care about others Here's the benefits copy and pasted from Piper's original message about it: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/796057759858425866/864927936610959440 "- the ability to only use the parts you care about.... stateless clients that only care about validating blocks could only be part of new block gossip..... miners could choose to only participate in tx gossip.... - keep differently shaped data stored separately..... 1 billion transactions vs 12 million block bodies... canonical transaction index data is way less important that chain history data so we probably don't want to apply the same eviction rules to them...." Ah! Thanks. Seems like we could cram all the key-value stores into one DHT, and just disambiguate when requesting the value. Or am I wrong in assuming that "most" participants in one portal network will participate in all portal networks? <@364458974906548225> have you already linked to those docs you shared in the call earlier? I wanted to look over them later but wasn't sure which link to look at <@!403636673914863626> https://notes.ethereum.org/h58LZcqqRRuarxx4etOnGQ
